column1: # The recovery after the Places correction: every execution of its three builds, which all run one
# frozen commit (build 2 correction, the correction gate; build 3 sweep; build 4 regressions), and the
# earlier execution each one counts as. Build 1, the first correction build (Codemagic 6ab8adb4, on
# 907d7401), passed 14 of its 15 required rows (C12 failed on a product issue); it ran an earlier
# commit and an earlier manifest, so it counts toward nothing here. Its rows are the manifest's rows of
# those scopes (docs/verification/places-review-manifest.tsv), by build and in manifest order within
# each; scripts/places_recovery_reconcile.py checks this file against the manifest and joins the three
# Columns (tab-separated): row, build, scope, device, run, test, kind, covers.
#   row      the manifest row ID in the scope that executes it.
#   device   main = the selected iPhone 17 Pro Max; small = the smaller iPhone; b = device B, a clone of main.
#   kind     as in the manifest: required, or repeat (B14, optional). Only required rows count as coverage.
#            The scroll probe's diagnostic rows C16 and C17 were removed from the manifest after build
#   covers   the earlier execution it counts as, <scope>:<row> of the places, signal or regressions scope,
#            or "-" for a check that has no earlier row (the correction's own tests).
# The identity rule: an execution counts as an earlier one only when it is the same test method, on the
# same device class, in the same run type (a recorded "journey" run keeps full holds; every other run
# uses short holds), at the same frozen commit as the other two builds. By that rule P7 = C9, P8 = C15,
# S1 = C4, S2 = C5, S7 = C6, S11 = C7 and S14 = C8; the other 49 of the 56 earlier required executions
# (13 places, 16 signal, 27 regressions) keep their own IDs in the sweep (P1-P6, P9-P13 and S3-S6, S8-S10,
# S12, S13, S15, S16) and in regressions, which is the regressions scope itself, unchanged. 64 required
